title: Everything through Tor
description: Every connection of the sandbox and of its MCP servers, the agent's own API connections included, leaves through Tor; lookups go to Tor's resolver and .onion names work. Checked before the agent starts and again during the run: an address that is no Tor exit stops it. The allow-list, approvals and the connection proxy apply as always.

de.title: Alles über Tor
de.description: Jede Verbindung der Sandbox und ihrer MCP-Server, auch die API-Verbindungen des Agenten, geht über Tor; Namen löst Tors Resolver auf, .onion-Namen funktionieren. Geprüft vor dem Start des Agenten und erneut während des Laufs: eine Adresse, die kein Tor-Exit ist, beendet ihn. Freigabeliste, Rückfragen und der Verbindungs-Proxy gelten wie immer.

tor.label: Tor profile (sandbox-ai vpn list)
tor.hint: once: sandbox-ai build tor; sandbox-ai vpn add anon --tor --socks (--bridges FILE for obfs4 bridges, --exit-country CC)

notes: Make the profile once: sandbox-ai build tor (the Tor container's image), then sandbox-ai vpn add anon --tor --socks (--bridges FILE for obfs4 bridges, --exit-country de); sandbox-ai vpn check anon tries it alone. The value must name a Tor profile (another type of VPN profile is refused, a --vpn of another type on the command line too).

Before the agent starts tor must bootstrap, check.torproject.org must see a Tor exit, and tor's resolver must answer and map an .onion name; a failed check stops the start. During the run the exit is checked again (a minute after the start, then every 10 minutes): an address that is no Tor exit ends the run. --vpn-check warn is refused with this preset.

The MCP servers of the start that reach the network run behind the same Tor (each in a Tor container of its own, checked as the agent's); a server with a VPN of another type is refused, so is one that runs already without Tor (sandbox-ai mcp stop NAME first).

Nothing of the start reaches your own address: no URL of the agent opens in your browser (open it in Tor Browser), names allowed during the run are looked up through Tor, and the host's ports (--allow-host-port, an --llm server on this host, a Git server on localhost) are refused, since whatever listens there reaches the internet from your address; --vpn-bypass-host-ports lets them in when you mean it. An --llm server in your local network cannot be reached (Tor's exits refuse private addresses).
TCP over IPv4 only: no UDP (no QUIC, ping or NTP) and no IPv6; slower than without, and many sites, the agent's provider among them, may refuse or challenge Tor exits.
.onion names resolve into 10.192.0.0/10 and connect through Tor; with --dns (set here) every .onion the agent looks up, not only those of its allow-list.

With --socks in the profile (sandbox-ai vpn add NAME --tor --socks), 127.0.0.1:9050 in the sandbox is Tor's SocksPort for programs that speak SOCKS (curl --socks5-hostname, torsocks, Tor Browser with TOR_SKIP_LAUNCH=1); what goes through it passes the connection proxy by. torsocks and Tor Browser in the agent's image: sandbox-ai images recipe tor --from AGENT && sandbox-ai build --variant tor, then add --image-variant tor.
The exit relay sees what is not encrypted: use HTTPS. Podman only (the tunnel runs in a container of the pod).
